# prd-to-jira-issues — Reference

Detailed contracts and conventions for the three deterministic scripts and the human-in-the-loop slice plan. See [SKILL.md](SKILL.md) for the high-level workflow and [EXAMPLES.md](EXAMPLES.md) for worked end-to-end runs.

## Child description template

Every child Task or Technical Story carries this body (rendered into the slice plan's `description: |` block, then passed verbatim to Atlassian's `createJiraIssue`):

```markdown
## What to build (in <component>)

<one-line scope>

## Background (auto-snapshot from parent — do not edit)

<Problem Statement from parent>

**<component> impact**:
- <component>: <bullet from parent's Cross-Application Impact>

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] <testable criterion 1; mention the suggested test type (unit / integration / e2e)>
- [ ] <testable criterion 2>
- [ ] <testable criterion 3>

## Implementation Hints (graphify-derived)

- Modules to touch: <comma-separated module names>

## Out of Scope (this slice)

- <handled by sibling slice if applicable>

## Blocked by

- Slice <letter>  *(omit when none — render `None — can start immediately`)*

## User stories addressed

- User story <N> (from parent <PARENT-KEY>)
```

Research and Design slices replace `## What to build` with `## Investigation` and a single instruction sentence.

## Slice plan markdown format

The output of `propose_slices.py` and the input to `write_jira_children.py`. Lives at `redlines/<parent-key>.md` (gitignored). Parsed by [`scripts/write_jira_children.py`](scripts/write_jira_children.py) using shared helpers in [`.agents/skills/_lib/markdown.py`](../_lib/markdown.py).

```markdown
# Slice plan for <PARENT-KEY>: <parent summary>

> Generated by propose_slices.py from <PARENT-KEY> + graphify on <ISO-8601 minute>.
> Edit freely: ...

## Slice A — <component>: <one-liner>
- type: Task                        # Task | Technical Story | Research | Design
- title: [BE] <full title>          # exact summary used at createJiraIssue time
- component: payment-platform       # one of the 4 canonical repos
- depends_on: (none)                # or `B` or `B, C`. Letters reference siblings in this file.
- modules: ProcessorHealthClient    # graphify-derived; informational
- user_stories: 1, 2, 3             # parent user-story indices this slice addresses
- description: |
  ## What to build...
  <indented body>
```

### Parser rules (enforced by `parse_keyvalue_block` + `validate_slices`)

- One section per child issue. Section header must match `## Slice <UPPER> — <text>`.
- Required keys per slice: `type`, `title`, `component`, `depends_on`, `description`. Optional: `modules`, `user_stories`.
- `type` values: `Task`, `Technical Story`, `Research`, `Design`. Trailing space on `Research`/`Design` is optional in the redline; the script always emits the trailing-space form to Atlassian.
- `component` values: `payment-platform`, `walletapi`, `infrastructure`, `spring-boot-starters`. Anything else fails validation.
- `depends_on` values: `(none)`, empty, a single letter, or comma-separated letters. References must point at slices defined in the same file. Self-references fail.
- `description: |` indentation is detected from the first content line. Subsequent lines must keep that indent. Trailing blank lines under the block are stripped.
- `TODO` is a reserved literal. Any description containing it fails validation (the placeholder gate for acceptance criteria).

## Action-plan JSON contracts

All three scripts emit JSON to stdout. The LLM agent in chat is the executor — none of the scripts call MCP tools directly.

### `validate_parent.py`

Three-phase output. Status field tells the LLM which phase emitted the plan.

```json
// Phase 1: needs_fetch_parent
{
  "status": "needs_fetch_parent",
  "actions": [{"step": 1, "tool": "atlassian.getJiraIssue", "args": {"issueKey": "PLTPM-21500"}}],
  "next_step": "Save the response to a JSON file and re-invoke ..."
}

// Phase 2: needs_fetch_confluence
{
  "status": "needs_fetch_confluence",
  "confluence_url": "https://...",
  "actions": [{"step": 1, "tool": "atlassian.getConfluencePage", "args": {"url": "..."}}]
}

// Phase 3: validated parent (the input to propose_slices.py)
{
  "status": "ok",
  "key": "PLTPM-21500",
  "summary": "...",
  "issue_type": "Story",
  "components": ["payment-platform"],
  "primary_component": "payment-platform",
  "is_elevated": false,
  "confluence_url": null,
  "description": "...",
  "full_prd_text": "...",
  "sections": {"Problem Statement": "...", ...}
}
```

Exit codes: `0` (any phase emitted), `1` (validation failed — `status: "invalid"` on stdout), `2` (IO/parse error — message on stderr).

### `propose_slices.py`

Two-phase output.

```json
// Phase 1: needs_graphify
{
  "status": "needs_graphify",
  "actions": [
    {"step": 1, "tool": "graphify.search", "args": {"text": "..."}, "purpose": "..."},
    {"step": 2, "tool": "graphify.get_node", "args": {"id": "<PER_HIT>"}, "purpose": "..."},
    {"step": 3, "tool": "graphify.get_edges", "args": {"from_id": "<EACH_HIT>"}, "purpose": "..."}
  ],
  "next_step": "Aggregate responses into {modules, edges} JSON ..."
}

// Phase 2: render-mode summary (the markdown is in `path`)
{
  "status": "ok",
  "slice_count": 3,
  "types": {"Task": 2, "Research": 1},
  "ordering_edges": [{"from": "A", "to": "B"}],
  "letters": ["A", "B", "C"],
  "path": "redlines/PLTPM-21500.md"
}
```

Exit codes: `0` (success), `2` (IO/parse), `3` (output path exists; pass `--force` to overwrite).

Graphify fixture shape (consumed in phase 2):

```json
{
  "modules": [{"name": "TransferSaga", "repo": "payment-platform"}, ...],
  "edges": [{"from": "TransferSaga", "to": "WalletLedgerClient", "type": "calls"}, ...]
}
```

### `write_jira_children.py`

Single-phase output. The action plan is deterministic and ordered into 4 phases:

| Phase | Tool | Per slice | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `atlassian.createJiraIssue` | 1 | Stores child key as `slice_<letter>_key`. |
| 2 | `atlassian.createJiraSubtask` | 5 | Skipped for `Research`/`Design`. Names: `Development`, `Code Review 1`, `Code Review 2`, `Test case creation`, `Test case execution`. Empty descriptions. |
| 3 | `atlassian.createIssueLink` (`Implement`) | 1 | `inwardIssue=parent`, `outwardIssue={{slice_<letter>_key}}`. |
| 4 | `atlassian.createIssueLink` (`Blocks`) | 0..N | One per `depends_on` entry. `inwardIssue={{blocker}}`, `outwardIssue={{blocked}}` per `.agents/jira-conventions.md` directionality. |

Steps are 1-indexed and consecutive. Each `createJiraIssue` action carries `stores_as`. Each later step references prior keys via the `{{slice_<letter>_key}}` placeholder; the agent substitutes after each `createJiraIssue` returns.

Exit codes: `0` (plan emitted), `1` (slice plan invalid — `status: "invalid"` on stdout), `2` (IO error).

## Atlassian MCP call patterns

Per `.agents/jira-conventions.md`:

- `createJiraIssue` — fields needed: `projectKey` (`PLTPM` for gru), `issueType`, `summary`, `description`, `components` (array of `{name}`).
- `createJiraSubtask` — fields needed: `parentIssueKey`, `summary`, `description`. Field defaults inherit from the parent issue.
- `createIssueLink` — fields needed: `type` (one of `Implement`, `Blocks`), `inwardIssue`, `outwardIssue`. **Directionality**: inward = blocker / parent; outward = blocked / child.
- `Research ` and `Design ` issue types have a trailing space — the action plan emits them with the space; do not strip whitespace from `args.issueType`.

## Graphify access (via harness helper)

The script emits the same generic three-step action plan it always did; what changed is how the agent resolves it. Each `graphify.<intent>` action translates to a shell exec of `.agents/skills/_lib/graphify.py` (no graphify MCP server is required):

- `graphify.search` → `python _lib/graphify.py search --text "<implementation-decisions text>"` — substring search over node `norm_label` / `label`. Returns `[{id, label, repo, score}, ...]`. Pass `text` derived from the parent's `## Implementation Decisions` section.
- `graphify.get_node` → `python _lib/graphify.py get_node --id <hit-id>` — returns the node augmented with a derived `repo` field (first path segment of `source_file`). Required for the `modules` array.
- `graphify.get_edges` → `python _lib/graphify.py get_edges --from-id <hit-id>` — outbound edges only, normalised to `{from, to, type}`. Required for the `edges` array.

One-shot convenience (recommended for `propose_slices.py`'s phase-1 → phase-2 handoff): `python _lib/graphify.py aggregate --text "..." [--scope-repos a b ...]` returns the `{modules, edges}` fixture directly. Pass back via `--graphify-fixture`.

Default graph: `~/payments-graph/graphify-out/graph.json` (override via `$GRAPHIFY_GRAPH_JSON`). When no graph.json is reachable, `aggregate` returns `{"status": "needs_synthesis", "reason": ..., "hint": ...}` instead of raising, so the SKILL falls back to PRD-only fixture synthesis (the F1 manual workaround). See "Harness helpers" in gru's `AGENTS.md` for the full helper contract.

## Idempotency limitation (Issue 5B locked decision)

`write_jira_children.py` does not journal which actions have already succeeded. On partial failure, the agent re-runs the script and the LLM filters already-succeeded actions from chat context (the LLM has the full transcript including prior `createJiraIssue` responses).

This is acceptable for the PoC because:
- Each script's output is deterministic for the same input — re-running mid-flight produces the same plan.
- Most failures are transient (network, rate limits) and the agent can resume.
- The cost of an over-creation (e.g. duplicate Sub-task) is low — operations can delete via the Jira UI.

It is **not** acceptable for production-grade automation. If re-runs cause real pain, revisit by adding a marker file (e.g. `redlines/<parent-key>.completed.json`) that records `{tool, args_hash → result_key}` and is consulted on re-entry.

## Failure modes

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `validate_parent.py` exits 1 with `Story or Technical Story` | Parent is `Epic` or `Bug` | Drop `prd-to-jira-issues`; this skill only operates on `write-a-prd` outputs. |
| Exits 1 with `required PRD section(s) missing` | Parent description was hand-written, missing some of the 8 sections | Edit the parent description in Jira to add the missing sections. |
| Exits 1 with `expected exactly one canonical Component` | Parent has 0 or ≥2 Components | Manually fix the parent. The `.agents/jira-conventions.md` "Components policy" requires exactly 1 per gru ticket. |
| `propose_slices.py` exits 3 with `already exists` | Pre-existing redline file for this parent | Inspect; pass `--force` only if you want to overwrite the file (and lose any in-progress edits). |
| `write_jira_children.py` exits 1 with `literal TODO` | PM/eng forgot to fill in acceptance criteria | Open the redline, replace the `<!-- TODO ... -->` placeholder + stub bullets with real ACs. |
| Exits 1 with `unknown slice 'Z'` | `depends_on:` references a letter not present | Either rename a slice or remove the dangling dependency. |
| Some slice creates but Sub-tasks fail | Atlassian rate limit or transient error | Re-run `write_jira_children.py`; the LLM filters succeeded steps from context (Issue 5B). |

## Maintenance

- `CANONICAL_COMPONENTS` in `validate_parent.py` and `propose_slices.py` and `write_jira_children.py` must stay in lockstep with `.agents/jira-conventions.md`. The sentinel test in `tests/test_validate_parent.py::TestCanonicalComponentsLocked` enforces this.
- `_lib/markdown.py` is shared with `write-a-prd`. Refactors there must keep both skills' tests green (`(cd .agents/skills/write-a-prd/scripts && pytest)` and `(cd .agents/skills/prd-to-jira-issues/scripts && pytest)`).
- `CEREMONY_SUBTASKS` in `write_jira_children.py` mirrors `.agents/jira-conventions.md` lines 188-194. Update both together.
